actions.name: Occurs in at least one protected area

documentation.range: This species is known from western and northern Colombia and northwestern Venezuela. In Colombia, it occurs in the Cauca and Magdalena river basins in the departments of Antioquia, Atlántico, Bolívar, Caldas, Córdoba, Cesar, Magdalena, Norte de Santander, Tolima, Santander, Sucre, and Valle del Cauca. In Venezuela, it has been recorded around the Maracaibo Lake Bain in Zulia state. It ranges up to 1,000 m asl. It is suggested to occur in the Orinoco River and Trinidad, although this requires confirmation.
documentation.population: It is considered to be a very common species.
documentation.habitats: This aquatic species inhabits rivers, marshes, and lakes, usually in open areas, and is only rarely found on land. It thrives in polluted water and is resilient to major water quality degradation. It is ovoviviparous, giving birth to young in the water.
documentation.threats: It is extremely resilient to habitat degradation and pollution, both of which are extensive within its range. It is popular in the international pet trade, but not at a level to constitute a threat to the species.
documentation.measures: It is present in several protected areas throughout its range (IUCN and UNEP-WCMC 2020).
documentation.use_trade: It is the most commonly traded caecilian. There is a small trade in captive-born animals.
documentation.rationale: Listed as Least Concern in view of its wide distribution, tolerance of a significant level of habitat degradation, and presumed large and stable population.
